reviews.title: I am a victim of fraud
reviews.body:
I reported suspected fraudulent activity after receiving multiple verification codes relating to attempts to transfer my number to another SIM. Two attempted payments of £30 were declined, followed by three successful £5 payments using the card saved to my Lebara account. I did not authorise any of this.

I contacted my bank immediately and notified Lebara the following day. Lebara initially reassured me that my number had not been transferred and described the messages as spam. After my bank recovered the unauthorised £15, Lebara barred my calls, texts and mobile data because of the chargeback. I was told to reverse it or purchase a £15 PAYG voucher—even though I have never bought PAYG vouchers and normally only pay for my monthly plan and data add-ons.

I have now been without service for six days, despite continuing to pay for a plan I cannot use. Lebara has not explained how the activity occurred, whether my account or number was compromised, what investigation was conducted, or what steps have been taken to secure my account.

The impact has been serious. I rely on my phone for community-based work and to care for disabled family members. When my disabled mother recently had a fall, I was unable to contact her carers to update them because my service remained barred.

Lebara repeatedly refers to its own “financial loss”, but what about the financial loss, distress and disruption suffered by its customer? I have sent numerous emails to Customer Care, the Complaints Team and the CEO. Key questions have been ignored, and Lebara has still not provided the deadlock letter I repeatedly requested. The CEO Stephen Shurrock or Business Operatioin Director John Paul Patten does not care 

Lebara should have secured my account, investigated the unusual payment and SIM-transfer activity, confirmed whether my information was compromised and maintained or temporarily restored my service while investigating.

I am still waiting for my service to be restored, a full explanation, reimbursement for the paid service I have been unable to use, appropriate compensation and either a proper resolution or a deadlock letter.

Anyone thinking of using them avoid and if you have an ongoing complaint complain to the ombudsman!
